problem: LLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav methods prompt with only local or object-only cues (or a metric frontier map) and lack structured region/topology information. Existing scene graphs have fixed structures tailored to one environment type and often depend on metric SLAM, so they do not generalise across environments, sensors and robots.
motivation: Open-world semantic navigation needs foundation models (LLMs, VFMs, general navigation models) plus a scene representation acting as working memory that is structured for LLM reasoning and works across environment types. Region-level context (e.g. a dining room hinting at a nearby kitchen) is vital for locating targets, especially when few object cues are visible.
key_idea: Open Scene Graphs: a configurable, topo-semantic, hierarchical scene graph (objects, connectors, places, region abstractions) built online purely by prompting VFMs and LLMs from a per-environment-type spec, used inside the zero-shot OpenSearch system for open-world ObjectNav.
insight: Giving the LLM region and topology information in addition to objects improves search: OS-GT beats LFG-GT (SR 0.775 vs 0.675) and LFG-GT beats object-only LGX-GT (0.275), and qualitative cases show gains when object cues are sparse. Reasoning quality depends heavily on LLM capability: replacing GPT-3.5 with Llama-2 7B/13B cuts SR from 0.693 to 0.349/0.538. The OSG spec lets the same mapper produce homes, supermarkets, offices and malls without retraining.
method: OSG meta-structure: layers for Objects (required), Connectors (optional), Places (required) and Region Abstractions (optional), with 'is near', 'connects to' and 'contains' edges; instantiated per environment type via a JSON OSG spec

Image Parser: BLIP-2 VQA labels the current Place type, GroundingDINO detects objects and connectors, an LLM classifies detections into spec classes, and BLIP-2 describes colour and material; proximity comes from pixel-distance thresholds

State Estimator: an LLM finds Place nodes with similar labels, then does pairwise place matching by comparing 'object features' (descriptions of nearby objects) to recognise the current Place without metric pose

OSG Updater: an LLM associates new observations with existing leaf nodes via object features, adds new Place and leaf nodes, and infers upper-layer Region Abstractions (e.g. floors, sections) with prompts

Reasoner: few-shot, chain-of-thought LLM prompted with the OSG JSON, goal and history; Region Proposer descends top-down through layers to pick a Place (or a Connector to explore new areas), Goal Proposer picks an Object/Connector, and a Dijkstra Pathfinder over the OSG handles replanning

Controller: MoveToObject uses the ViNT general navigation model zero-shot with stored object image crops as image goals, with adaptive thresholding of temporal distance for stopping; the simulation experiments use an FMM planner with depth and GT pose

setting.backbone: GPT-3.5 (frozen LLM) + BLIP-2 (VQA) + GroundingDINO (detector) + ViNT (image-goal navigation policy, real world)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; all foundation models used zero-shot)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (depth and GT pose only used by the FMM controller in simulation)
setting.action_space: high-level MoveToObject/MoveToRegion executed as velocity commands; in simulation FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° via FMM
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson, HM3D-Semantics v0.1) plus real world
setting.privileged: Simulation FMM controller uses depth and ground-truth pose; the OS-GT variant uses GT semantic annotations; the main OS variant uses none for perception

Real-world results are success counts out of 5 trials (Spot: guitar 4/5, dish washer 5/5; Fetch: guitar 4/5, dish washer 4/5). The ablation over LLMs (Table 9, 100 episodes): Llama 2 7B SR 0.349, 13B 0.538, GPT-3.5 0.693.
results: OpenSearch zero-shot reaches SR 0.734 / SPL 0.386 on Gibson, competitive with trained PONI (0.736 / 0.410) and better than training-free SemUtil (0.693 / 0.405 on SR/SPL, SR higher for OS). On HM3D it gets SR 0.693, far above the LLM baseline LFG-GT (0.675 with GT semantics) and LGX-GT (0.275), and OS-GT reaches 0.775. It also works on two real robots (Spot, Fetch) and on rare and compositional queries.
limitations: Slow and costly: 0.5-2 minutes per update/planning step due to many GPT-3.5 calls; smaller LLMs degrade a lot

No handling of uncertainty and no metric information, causing place mis-segmentation (over-segmenting hallways, mislabelling hallways as living rooms); SPL suffers because topological search does not optimise geometric paths
Real-world evaluation is small (5 trials per goal in one apartment) and the GNM (ViNT) fails in cluttered areas
